description: API-shape experiment for clip launching (session view). The same six tasks are given with no API (desire mode) or with one variant's type declarations only (guess mode). Expectations are variant-agnostic: they describe behaviour, not names.

tasks.prompt: A browser session view has a Bass track with two looping audio clips, A and B (both AudioBuffers you already have), at 120 BPM in 4/4. Bass is playing clip A. When the user clicks clip B, B must start exactly on the next bar line and A must stop at that same instant. Start the transport from a button click (browser autoplay rules apply).
expectations: Starts or resumes the audio context inside the click handler (or calls an API documented as doing so).
Clip B is scheduled at the next bar boundary computed from the transport (4 beats at 120 BPM), not immediately and not with setTimeout.
Clip A stops at the same audio time B starts (no gap, no overlap beyond what the API defines).

tasks.prompt: Launch a scene: Drums clip 2, Bass clip 2 and Keys clip 2 must all start together on the next bar, sample-aligned, replacing whatever each of those tracks was playing. A fourth track, Vocals, must keep playing untouched.
expectations: Queues all three track changes so they share one start time (a single launch call or three calls that land on the same boundary).
The start time is the next bar boundary from the transport.
Vocals is not part of the launch and keeps playing.

tasks.prompt: The user queued Bass clip B for the next bar, then clicks it again before the bar line. That second click must withdraw the queued launch so that clip A keeps playing without any interruption. Other tracks' queued launches must stay queued.
expectations: Withdraws only the Bass launch before its boundary.
Clip A keeps playing with no gap or restart.
Other tracks' pending launches are not cancelled.

tasks.prompt: Add per-track stop buttons and a Stop All button. A track's stop takes effect on the next bar line (the track falls silent there); Stop All silences every track on the next bar line. The transport itself keeps running.
expectations: A track stop is quantized to the next bar boundary and silences only that track.
Stop All is quantized to the next bar boundary and silences every track.
The transport is not stopped by either button.

tasks.prompt: Drums has a one-bar fill clip. Launching it should play it once, starting on the next bar, and then the Drums track should go back to silence when the fill ends (not loop).
expectations: Launches the fill as a one-shot (plays once) rather than a loop.
It starts on the next bar boundary.
When it ends the track is silent; the code does not schedule a manual stop with setTimeout.

tasks.prompt: Add a global quantize select with options: none (start immediately), 1 beat, 1 bar, 2 bars. Every clip or scene launch uses the selected quantize. Show, for each queued clip, the exact audio time it will start.
expectations: 'none' launches at the current audio time (no boundary wait).
1 beat / 1 bar / 2 bars map to 1 / 4 / 8 beats at 4/4 and the launch waits for that boundary.
The displayed start time is the audio-context time returned or exposed by the launch, not a separately recomputed estimate.
